items.topic: EPUB metadata in the supply chain
items.proposed_text: Intermediaries and retailers can use accessibility metadata embedded in the EPUB package document, external ONIX records, or both. ONIX also supports exchange before publication. Keep the information consistent across formats.
items.evidence: W3C Display Guide 2.1 section 1.2 explicitly describes internal and external metadata and vendor choice.

items.proposed_text: For a publication that claims conformance to EPUB Accessibility 1.1, include the specified dcterms:conformsTo statement and identify the evaluator with a11y:certifiedBy, in addition to the required discovery metadata above. The evaluator may be the publisher; this field does not by itself mean independent certification.
items.reason: Remove the distracting ONIX opening. Avoid implying all EPUBs with discovery metadata can or must claim accessibility conformance. W3C EPUB Accessibility 1.1 distinguishes discovery and accessible-publication conformance.

items.decision: Clarify distinction; do not adopt a blanket either-format-is-legally-sufficient claim.
items.proposed_text: EPUB Accessibility conformance and compliance with applicable accessibility law are separate questions. Metadata format choice alone does not establish that the publication and service meet all applicable requirements.
items.next_action: Verify exact legal wording before publication, including national rules and actual delivery/discoverability of metadata. EUR-Lex returned a robot challenge in this pass.
